stem.en: A cell measures about 2 µm across. It has a cell membrane, cytoplasm and a cell wall, and its genetic material lies in a region with no membrane around it. How should it be classified?

text.en: Eukaryotic, because a cell with a membrane and a wall must also count as a true cell.

feedback.en: Having a membrane and a wall does not decide this. Prokaryotic cells have both.

text.en: Prokaryotic, because its genetic material is not enclosed.
Not a cell at all, because a true cell must always have a well-defined nucleus inside it.

feedback.en: It has a membrane and cytoplasm and it is a cell. Bacteria have no well-defined nucleus.

text.en: Eukaryotic, because cells that measure 2 µm across are too small to be prokaryotic.

feedback.en: Prokaryotic cells are typically 1 to 10 µm across, so 2 µm fits them well.

explanation.en: A nucleoid has no membrane around it, and that makes this cell prokaryotic. Its size, 2 µm, also fits the usual range of 1 to 10 µm.

hints.en: Is the genetic material enclosed by a membrane?
